question.leadin: Answer these questions about court cases concerning African American rights.
question.text: Brown v. Board of Education overturned Plessy v. Ferguson, which allowed for segregation by establishing this three word doctrine.
question.clue: This three-word doctrine. Almost sixty years afterPlessy, this doctrine was partially thrownout in acase against the Topeka Board of Education.

swap.text: One year after Stonewall, the first of these public events took place. These events celebrate the progress of the LGBT community and often feature people waving rainbow flags as they march down streets.
swap.answerHtml: Pride parades (accept additional information, such as Gay Pride parades; prompt on partial answers)
swap.clue: The largest annual one of these events in the world first started in New York after the Stonewall Riots and attracted 4 million visitors in 2019. These events express solidarity with the LGBTQ+ community.

question.text: As president, Johnson launched this series of programs that included Medicare and Medicaid. Its most famous part was the "War on Poverty" that led to the Economic Opportunity Act.
question.clue: This plan was depicted as an improvement on being just "rich" or "powerful" in a speech at the University of Michigan in 1964.

swap.text: This man's campaign used the slogan "In your guts, you know he's nuts" to mock Goldwater's slogan. This president defeated Goldwater in 1964 after succeeding Kennedy.
swap.clue: In the Senate, he perfected a strategy of intimidation that involved standing uncomfortably close known as "The Treatment."

question.text: This Supreme Court case ruled that states must provide attorneys for criminal defendants if they are unable to afford one. This case's namesake had been arrested for stealing items from a pool hall.
question.clue: Losing attorney Bruce Jacob stated that his strategy in this case was to tie it to Betts v. Brady, which was overturned by this case.

swap.text: Name this president who created Medicare and Medicaid through his Great Society program as part of his war on poverty.
swap.clue: During a speech at the University of Michigan, this president announced an initiative that produced a program supporting low-income children called Head Start.

question.text: This governor served three consecutive terms, and was nominated by both major parties in 1946. As Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, he presided over Miranda v. Arizona and Brown v. Board of Education.
question.clue: As a popular governor of California, he became the losing running mate of Thomas Dewey in 1948.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the gay rights movement.
swap.text: These riots at their namesake Greenwich Village inn are considered the start of the gay rights movement in America.
swap.clue: This event took place at a business owned by the Genovese crime family.

question.leadin: The symbol for this organization was chosen to contrast with a white rooster that represented white supremacy, as well as as an homage to the Lowndes County Freedom Organization.
question.text: Name this organization founded by two men who met at Merritt College, Huey Newton and Bobby Seale.
question.clue: The Free Breakfast for Children program was founded by that U.S. group of this name, which was targeted by the Mulford Act to discourage its members' armed patrols of Oakland, which they called "copwatching."

swap.text: This future Supreme Court Justice was a Klan member until 1926. This ardent defender of absolute free speech wrote the majority opinion in Korematsu v. US.
swap.clue: Ray Springle wrote a series of investigative articles which revealed that this justice was a former member of the KKK. This justice from Alabama wrote the majority opinion of Korematsu v. U.S.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about an event that began after the raiding of a "blind pig," the 1967 Detroit riot.
question.text: LBJ appointed this commission to determine the causes of the Detroit riot and other 1960's race riots. It included John Lindsay and Edward Brooke and was named after its chair, a governor of Illinois.
question.clue: It warned that "Our nation is moving towards two societies ... separate and unequal" and declared that "white society is deeply implicated in the ghetto."

swap.text: This executive director of the NAACP refused to allow any public recognition for activist Bayard Rustin, probably because of Rustin's suspected homosexuality. This University of Minnesota graduate had previously replaced W.E.B. DuBois as editor of the magazine Crisis.
swap.clue: This St. Louis-born leader of the NAACP, who served as that organization's executive director throughout the height of the civil rights movement, beginning in 1955.

question.leadin: Answer the following about people or things disliked by former senator Strom Thurmond.
question.text: Thurmond led the Senate effort to defeat the nomination of this man as Chief Justice. This jurist earlier served as the defense attorney in the case of Gideon v. Wainwright.
question.clue: When Lyndon Johnson tried to elevate him to Chief Justice, a filibuster by a bipartisan coalition in the Senate forced the President to withdraw his nomination. He later resigned from the Court after a financial scandal.

swap.text: This 1968 presidential candidate was offered a guest spot on Laugh-In, but declined. This man became paralyzed after being shot by Arthur Bremer on a 1972 campaign stop.
swap.clue: During this man's 1972 presidential run with former Air Force general Curtis LeMay, he was shot and paralyzed by Arthur Bremer.

question.leadin: In this case, Tom C. Clark wrote, "Nothing can destroy a government more quickly than its failure to observe its own laws."
question.text: Name this landmark 1961 case that incorporated the exclusionary rule. This case included the discovery of "lewd and lascivious books and pictures."
question.clue: Justice Harlan's dissent claimed that there was no reason to reconsider the case of Wolf v. Colorado, while the majority opinion for this case was written by Thomas Clark.

swap.text: The 1948 case Morgan v. Virginia earlier outlawed segregation in some of these places. The segregation of these places was fully ruled unconstitutional in the case Browder v. Gayle.
swap.clue: The caseBrowder v. Gayledealtwith the desegregation of these things, whichare operatedby Trailways and Greyhound.

question.leadin: This organization is the subject of a 2020 book by CUNY professor Johanna Fernandez.
question.text: Name this organization that launched The People's Program to treat heroin addicts in the South Bronx after occupying part of the Lincoln Hospital. This revolutionary nationalist organization was founded by Jose "Cha Cha" Jimenez ("hee-MEN-ez").

swap.leadin: This group cited the writings of Michelle Wallace to argue that, if they had freedom, it would necessitate the destruction of oppression, as opposed to starting from below.
swap.text: Name this lesbian socialist collective whose members included Demita Frazier and Margo Okazawa-Rey. It took its name from an action taken by the 2nd South Carolina Infantry in June 1863.

question.leadin: This book argues that its main character divided society into elite "Franklins" who were resented by the striving middle-class "Orthogonians."
question.text: Name this book by Rick Perlstein that analyzes the "fracturing of America" during the 1960s through the rise of the title politician.
question.answerHtml: Nixonland [or Nixonland: The Rise of a President and the Fracturing of America]

swap.leadin: Critics of this legislation asked why more Catholic school students didn't become nuns.
swap.text: Name this eponymous initiative placed on the California ballot in 1978, which would have declared teachers who engaged in "public homosexual activity" to be "unfit for service."
